transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Lately I keep hearing things that no one else seems to hear, and it’s starting to really bother me at work and at home. It's gotten to the point where I just can't ignore it anymore, so my family suggested I come in.
How long have you been hearing these sounds or voices, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

Well, my general struggles have been slowly building for a little over two years now, but this specific voice started about three months ago. It crept up on me gradually, but now it has become a steady, everyday problem.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or prescription medications regularly, especially around the time these voices started?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs, and I rarely ever drink alcohol. I'm also not taking any regular prescription medications right now.
Along with hearing these voices, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel sad or down, but I have completely lost the drive to do things I used to love. I'll just sit with my bass in my lap or stare at my kayak in the garage without any motivation to actually play or go out. Even trying to have a simple conversation feels like way too much effort now, so I mostly stay quiet.
Have you recently felt like people are watching you, talking about you, or that your thoughts are being controlled or read by others?

Sometimes I do feel like people are talking about me, but that's mainly because the voice will say things like "They're talking about you" when my wife is on the phone. I don't feel like anyone is watching me, though, and I definitely don't feel like my thoughts are being read or controlled.
You mentioned having general struggles for over two years before the voice started. Could you describe what those struggles were like?

It really started when my daughter moved out and my wife got busy caring for her parents, and I just began losing interest in things I used to love like kayaking, playing bass, and my tech projects. I became very withdrawn and stopped participating in our usual family routines. I barely spoke at dinner because trying to engage in conversations just felt like too much effort.
Have you or those close to you noticed that you have trouble keeping your thoughts organized, or that your speech has become difficult for others to follow?

No, I haven't really noticed any trouble keeping my thoughts organized, and no one has mentioned that my speech is hard to follow. I just don't talk very much lately because it feels like too much effort, but when I do, I think I make sense.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt the exact opposite of down—such as having an unusually high level of energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling extremely active and excited for days?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I haven't felt unusually excited or full of energy, and my sleep has been pretty normal. If anything, I've just felt much more withdrawn and lacking in energy.
How have these voices and your lack of motivation affected your ability to perform your job or handle your daily responsibilities at home?

At work, my manager ended up cutting my hours after writing me up for holding up the register line and unsettling customers when I'd lose focus. At home, my wife and daughter mostly just leave me alone now because I hardly ever join in on conversations or make family plans anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent auditory hallucinations lasting for 3 months, preceded by a 2-year history of progressive negative symptoms including avolition, alogia, and social withdrawal. These symptoms have caused significant functional impairment at work (reduced hours) and home (social isolation). Mood disorders and substance use have been ruled out, meeting the criteria for Schizophrenia (F20).
